feed.author: Anna Vu
feed.title: Batch #3 Beechwood Milling: Custom Chamfer & Friction Testing
feed.content: We tested 4 different wood finishes this week. High-gloss polyurethane looks shiny on photos, but in real play it caused the blocks to stick together unpredictably when pulling from the middle levels. We settled on a bespoke double-sanded beeswax matte polish. It provides the signature buttery Jenga slide while maintaining a silky tactile warmth in your hand.

feed.author: Ishaan
feed.title: Firmware v2.4: Achieving Sub-80ms Tag Detection on the Dock
feed.content: The biggest headache with earlier prototypes was the delay between slamming a block on the reader and seeing the OLED prompt appear. If it takes more than 300ms, the physical party rhythm is interrupted. With our custom dual-antenna coil arrangement inside the dock and SPI bus tuning, we brought tag response time down to 78 milliseconds. It feels instantaneous.

feed.author: Shiva Manickam
feed.title: Why AI Game Creation Changes Everything
feed.content: Traditional board games are static. You play 3 times and memorize all the cards. With Jeemu's mobile companion, you can literally type "Spicy Date Night for couple celebrating 5th anniversary who love sushi" and our model populates 45 custom prompt blocks in 8 seconds. You sync it via Bluetooth to the dock once, then turn your phone OFF for the entire game.

chaos.author: Jack
chaos.content: Playtester Marcus tried to remove Block #45 using his elbows because the rule said "non-dominant limb". The entire 32-level tower collapsed into Anna's gin & tonic. 10/10 gameplay experience.

chaos.author: Shefali
chaos.content: New prompt submission approved for the "After Dark" expansion pack: "Call your most recent food delivery driver and thank them for changing your life, or finish your beverage." Who hurt the person who submitted this??

chaos.author: Yana C
chaos.content: Engineering note: Do NOT stack 45 blocks horizontally on the OLED dock to test "simultaneous read capability". It threw error code #420: "Too much wood on desk".

journey.author: Shiva & Jack
journey.title: Classic Jenga is great for 15 minutes, then gathers dust.
journey.description: We taped index cards with handwritten drinking dares to standard blocks. It was hilarious, but within 2 games the tape peeled. We asked: what if the physical wood could dynamically trigger ANY game mode digitally?

journey.author: Anna & Ishaan
journey.title: Drilling 45 blocks and frying two Arduino Nanos.
journey.description: We drilled cavities into beechwood blocks with a Dremel press and embedded 13.56MHz NFC tags with wood epoxy. The first reader was a messy cardboard box with an Arduino taped to it.

journey.milestone: Phase 3: The Custom Dock & Standalone OS
journey.author: Entire Team
journey.title: Zero phones at the table. Standalone hardware decision.
journey.description: Gamers hate staring at apps while playing tabletop games. We built the Jeemu Smart Box as a standalone game master with an amber OLED display and internal battery. Phone-free during play.
